description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Geller Gambit. Hold with 5...b5! or develop the bishop first.

drills.briefExplanation: 4...dxc4 5.e4 b5! 6.e5 Nd5 — take the pawn, hold it, and blockade.
drills.description: Black to play. White plays 4.Nc3 — take on c4 and hold with 5...b5!.
drills.explanation: The greedy defense: after 4...dxc4 5.e4, Black holds with 5...b5!. After 6.e5 Nd5 the knight blockades the pawn roller — the classic antidote to mobile centers. Black is a pawn up, the blockade is solid, and White's 'initiative' runs into a wall. Blockade before you counterattack.
drills.name: The b5 Blockade

drills.briefExplanation: 6...Bb7 7.Bxc4 e6 8.O-O Nbd7 — develop, solidify, castle, complete the setup.
drills.description: Black to play. White pushed 6.e5 — fianchetto the bishop and play 7...e6.
drills.explanation: The positional defense: after 6.e5 Black plays 6...Bb7!, developing with pressure on e4. After 7.Bxc4 e6 Black solidifies — the bishop eyes the center, the e6 pawn supports d5, and White's pawn roller is contained. Development and solidity beat the gambit's momentum.
drills.name: The Bb7 Development
